title: Interior routing protocols: RIP, OSPF and EIGRP

videos.script: In lesson 15 every route was typed by hand. A cable broke, and one router never found out. {{recap}} This lesson hands the job to the routers themselves. A routing protocol is a conversation between neighbours. Each one says what it can reach, and each one recalculates when something changes. {{talk}} The lab is four routers in a ring, with a computer behind two of them. At the start, they know only their own cables. {{ring}} You will run three protocols on the same ring, one after the other. RIP counts routers, and picks the path with the fewest. {{rip}} OSPF builds a map of the whole network on every router. It adds up a cost per cable, and here it picks the long way round, on purpose. {{ospf}} Then you will break a cable in the worst way, with the light still on, and count the seconds of lost traffic. {{break}} Last comes EIGRP, Cisco's protocol, and the backup path it tries to keep ready. {{eigrp}} By the end you should be able to read each protocol's tables, and say why it chose its path.
